design.representation: Each existing node vector gains one size_t pending counter; nested move-only BindingAdmission holds only its concrete runtime pointer.
design.invariant: L + P <= C, where L is node vector size, P is outstanding token count and C is capacity; exactly one active token per unit of P.
design.reserve: Checked L+P+1; vector reserve before counter increment; token return is nonthrowing.
design.legacy_bind: Existing validation/idempotence retained; every fresh append ensures capacity for L+P+1, preserving outstanding credits.
design.consume: Validate token/runtime/identity first; append pointer within proven capacity; decrement pending; empty token; no callback between append and decrement.
design.cancel: No native/object/vector-element access; decrement one active credit, empty token; no unbind, release, shrink or allocation.
design.moves: Noexcept transfer; move assignment first cancels destination credit; self-move no-op; source empty.
design.scene_identity: Existing raw-key/runtime validation and canonical transform/key uniqueness, with same-object idempotence consuming an unused credit by cancellation.
design.lifetime_identity: Existing scene/transform equality and duplicate transform checks; admitted overload additionally requires exact canonical scene attachment lookup and rejects duplicate actual key. Legacy identity checks are unchanged.
design.failed_consume: Check token activity/runtime before node identity getters. The rvalue reference aliases the caller token; std::move alone does not consume. Validation and diagnostic-exception construction precede mutation; failure leaves token active. Only successful append/commit or idempotent scene cancellation empties it; overload is not noexcept.
design.allocation_failure: Reserve or ordinary bind failure leaves bindings, pending count and tokens unchanged; earlier successful capacity increases may remain.
design.runtime_lifetime: Stable runtime address, delete copy/move; destructor terminates on outstanding tokens without visiting bindings; runtime outlives tokens and registered objects.
design.token_lifetime: Consumed/empty token may outlive runtime; active token may not. Tokens never own or borrow native storage or bound nodes.
design.reentrancy: Single owning thread; callbacks between completed operations may consume independently prepared credits. No reentry inside vector mutation, allocator reserve or identity getters. Ordinary callback bind can still allocate.

camera_handoff.preflight: Allocate persistent companion storage; reserve one scene and one lifetime credit before B3C800 native events; second-reserve failure cancels first credit.
camera_handoff.owner_overload: NativeCameraOwner(void*, size_t, NativeCameraEnvironment&, SceneAttachmentRuntime::BindingAdmission&&); same placement preparation/cleanup, admitted scene bind only.
camera_handoff.reference_overload: NativeCameraReference(NativeCameraOwner&, NativeCameraCompanionDisposal, GeneratedModelLifetimeRuntime::BindingAdmission&&); existing validation and no added retain, admitted lifetime bind only.
camera_handoff.construction: Consume scene credit after actual slot allocation and before native camera construction; consume lifetime credit after successful live camera construction and before helper camera publication.
camera_handoff.failure: Unused credits cancel only host reservations. Existing native cleanup and exact raw-slot-return duties remain explicit; published camera and companions survive later helper failure.
camera_handoff.retirement: Preserve native cleanup/scene forget, raw pool return, lifetime unbind, companion disposal. Ticket destruction after consume does not unregister.
camera_handoff.reuse_contract: Concrete pool return has no allocator/host callback; serialized terminal release completes lifetime unbind before a caller can reuse the slot. Normal immediate reuse after release is supported. No extra restriction is invented for already-unsupported concurrency or artificial API hooks; actual stale aliases still fail admitted duplicate-key validation.
camera_handoff.early_borrow_limit: Callbacks before reference bind cannot use a lifetime interface; existing unbound validation remains and an early-borrow provider requires separate evidence.
camera_handoff.viewport_boundary: Parallel viewport worker reports two persistent view slots per attempt, separate actual identity publication and terminal retirement. Node cancellation never retires views; viewport borrow proof is outside this packet.
